The dock's compact pill row: upstream hides the pills' labels (and with them their count chips) as soon as its own pill row no longer fits on one line, while the fork keeps the labelled pills at every width and only compacts on a phone. Upstream's trigger is a width measure inside the minified bundle that could not be recovered; a wrap-based rule measured on the fork fires on the wrong scenes (12 of 30 in one probe, 6 in the next), and hiding a pill's label also moves the harness's own dock clicks off their target, so the guess is worse than the divergence it records. Deliberate: the fork keeps labelled pills. Open item if the compact state is wanted.
